title: What does one orange cost?
premise: A six-dollar bag of three oranges has a unit price of two dollars per orange.
context: Mara wonders whether the six-dollar tag is for one orange; then divide the total across three oranges.
signature: Pocket Cutouts: bold irregular plum outlines, ivory paper, expressive brows, apricot focal shapes, teal shadows. No baked text.

cues.caption: The tag is tied to the whole bag.
The tag is tied to the whole bag.

cues.say: So what would just one orange cost?
Share the six dollars equally across all three.
The price for one? That's the unit price.
cues.caption: For one orange: the unit price.

orange.visual: One beautiful plump round bright orange with one small green leaf. Thick plum outline, crisp contour, illustration filling the center against completely flat neutral white.

panels.visual: A curious shopkeeper Mara in a plum apron stands BEHIND exactly ONE broad ochre kraft paper grocery bag centered on the counter. BOTH her hands rest behind that same bag, not holding any other bags. One relatively small ivory rectangular blank price tag hangs DIRECTLY from this ONE bag's upper right corner by a short teal bow; the tag is less than half the bag's width, clearly a price tag not another bag. Keep the tag's flat front face blank and big enough for two characters added later. The one bag's broad ochre body is visible below the bow. Mara's eyes are wide and inquisitive. NO additional bags, totes, handbags, handles, tags, oranges or lettering. Simple portrait composition.
panels.keep: Distinct tag face, open view of knot, stable front camera.
